text: {"resumen":"A Kerberos service ticket was requested for the honeytoken account svc_sql_backup from source IP 192.168.56.103 (Kali, the simulated attacker host in this lab) by user crojas@LAB.LOCAL. The ticket encryption type is 0x17 (RC4) and the request succeeded (failure code 0x0). This is a near-zero false positive indicator: svc_sql_backup exists only as a tripwire and should never be used legitimately.","razonamiento":"Rule 100212 is designed to fire on any ticket request for svc_sql_backup because that account has no legitimate use case. The request originated from the known attacker host (Kali 192.168.56.103) and succeeded, indicating the attacker has obtained or is attempting to use credentials for this honeytoken account. This maps to T1558.003 (Kerberoasting) and represents a confirmed compromise signal. The high rule level (12) and the documented context that svc_sql_backup should never be requested legitimately justify critical priority and high confidence.","prioridad":"critical","confianza":"high","mitre_id":"T1558.003","campos_sustento":["rule_id","event_id","src_ip","service_name","timestamp","raw_log"],"accion_sugerida":"escalate_tier2","verificaciones_sugeridas":["Confirm whether crojas@LAB.LOCAL account has been compromised or if credentials were stolen","Review all Kerberos ticket requests from 192.168.56.103 (Kali) in the past 24 hours to identify scope of compromise","Check for any successful logons by crojas@LAB.LOCAL from unexpected locations or times","Verify whether svc_sql_backup credentials have been exposed or if the account has been used for any actual service activity","Isolate or monitor 192.168.56.103 for further malicious activity pending approval","Review group memberships and privileges of crojas@LAB.LOCAL to assess blast radius"],"possible_prompt_injection":false}

{"resumen":"The built-in Administrator account read properties of the decoy account adm_backup_legacy (verified by GUID match). This is a high-signal indicator of account discovery activity, as the decoy exists only as a tripwire and should never be accessed legitimately.","razonamiento":"The alert shows event 4662 (object access) with decoy_verified=true, confirming that the subject Administrator accessed the specific GUID of the honeypot account adm_backup_legacy. The object GUID dd002ba1-3992-4539-bf9b-9ee77df0952d matches the decoy's registered objectGUID. The operation was a Read Property access from the domain controller (192.168.56.10, the DC). This is consistent with account discovery (T1087.002), though a single read can also result from a broad directory query. The built-in Administrator account performing this read is unusual and warrants investigation to determine whether this is an approved administrative action or reconnaissance by a compromised or rogue admin account.","prioridad":"high","confianza":"high","mitre_id":"T1087.002","campos_sustento":["rule_id","event_id","decoy_verified","object_name","subject_user","dest_ip","raw_log"],"accion_sugerida":"manual_review","verificaciones_sugeridas":["Confirm whether the built-in Administrator account legitimately accessed the decoy account or whether the account is compromised.","Check the Logon ID (0x5D6BE) to correlate this event with other activities from the same logon session on the DC or other hosts.","Review recent activity from the Administrator account for other signs of enumeration (queries to other decoy accounts, broad LDAP searches, or lateral movement).","Verify whether any tools or scripts running under the Administrator context would legitimately enumerate user accounts.","Check the timestamp (2026-11-19T05:46:54.949+0000) against the DC's audit logs for any concurrent suspicious activity."],"possible_prompt_injection":false}

{"resumen": "The built-in Administrator account read properties of the decoy account adm_backup_legacy (GUID dd002ba1-3992-4539-bf9b-9ee77df0952d) on the domain controller. The decoy_verified flag confirms this was a direct access to the tripwire account, not a false positive from a broad directory query.","razonamiento": "Rule 100230 with decoy_verified=true indicates a confirmed access to an account that exists only as a detection mechanism and should never be legitimately used. The subject is the built-in Administrator account (SID ending in -500), which is a high-value target for attackers performing account discovery. The operation was a Read Property access on the DC (192.168.56.10), consistent with T1087.002 (Account Discovery). While the Administrator account itself is privileged, an attacker who has compromised it would use it to enumerate other accounts and discover additional targets. This is high priority because the decoy was touched; confidence is high because decoy_verified=true eliminates the ambiguity of whether the read was incidental to a broader query.","prioridad": "high","confianza": "high","mitre_id": "T1087.002","campos_sustento": ["rule_id","event_id","decoy_verified","subject_user","dest_ip","object_name"],"accion_sugerida": "escalate_tier2","verificaciones_sugeridas": ["Confirm whether the Administrator account is currently compromised or if this access was authorized by the SOC for testing purposes.","Review the logon history of the Administrator account on 2026-11-19 to identify the source and context of the session that performed this read.","Check for other account discovery or enumeration activity from the same subject or host around the same timestamp.","Verify whether any other decoy or sensitive accounts were accessed in the same session.","Review recent changes to the Administrator account's password or group memberships."],"possible_prompt_injection": false}

{"resumen":"The built-in Administrator account added a user (Carlos Rojas) to the Domain Admins group on the domain controller. This is a high-signal privileged group membership change.","razonamiento":"Rule 100220 (event 4728) fires on membership additions to privileged groups such as Domain Admins. The alert shows the built-in Administrator (SID ending in 500) added Carlos Rojas (SID ending in 1107) to Domain Admins (SID ending in 512) on DC01 (192.168.56.10). No decoy_verified field is present, and the context provided does not document this change as an approved modification. Per the environment guidance, a member added to Domain Admins is one of the highest-signal events in AD and must be treated as critical unless clear evidence of approval exists. The subject (Administrator) and target (Carlos Rojas) are both real accounts in the domain; the action occurred on the DC. Without documented approval, this meets the threshold for critical priority and requires immediate human review.","prioridad":"critical","confianza":"high","mitre_id":"T1098","campos_sustento":["rule_id","event_id","timestamp","target_user","subject_user","dest_ip","raw_log"],"accion_sugerida":"escalate_tier2","verificaciones_sugeridas":["Confirm whether this Domain Admins addition was approved by IT leadership or change management (e.g., ticket, email authorization).","Verify the business justification for granting Carlos Rojas Domain Admins privileges.","Check the logon history of the Administrator account around 2026-11-19T06:51:01Z to confirm the action was initiated by an authorized administrator and not by a compromised account.","Review any other group membership changes or privilege escalations involving Carlos Rojas or Administrator in the past 24 hours.","If not approved, immediately remove Carlos Rojas from Domain Admins and investigate whether the Administrator account has been compromised."],"possible_prompt_injection":false}
